::: {.hero-block}

## JSC370 2026 Final Project

Internal migration — residents moving between and within Canadian provinces — reshapes local labour markets, housing demand, and public-service planning more immediately than international immigration, yet gets far less attention. This project asks two questions at the Census Metropolitan Area (CMA) level across 2001–2024:

- **Primary (prediction).** How much variance in CMA net interprovincial and intraprovincial migration rate (per 1,000 residents) can push–pull structural factors explain, and which model family generalises best out of time?
- **Secondary (inference).** Is the 2020–2024 COVID period associated with a structural shift in migration trend, beyond what push–pull conditions alone predict, and does it differ by CMA size?

:::

## Headline findings

1. **Tree models substantially outperform linear models** for both outcomes. Random Forest reaches holdout R² ≈ 0.42 for intraprovincial rate and ≈ 0.30 for interprovincial rate; OLS gets 0.22 and 0.03 respectively.
2. **Intraprovincial migration is more predictable** than interprovincial. Within-province flows track housing affordability and demographic structure cleanly; cross-provincial flows depend on shock-driven opportunities that structural features approximate less well.
3. **The COVID structural shift is detectable but non-linear.** The interprovincial year-trend drops significantly for large CMAs post-2020 (HC3 p = 0.04); the intraprovincial linear interaction is not significant (p = 0.14), but the GAM smooth shows a clear 2020–2022 dip and partial 2023 rebound.
4. **International in-migration negatively predicts intraprovincial net flows** (HC3 p < 10⁻¹⁸): CMAs receiving more international migrants tend to lose residents to other CMAs in the same province, consistent with a displacement mechanism.

## Data

All five source tables are from Statistics Canada, pulled programmatically via the bulk CSV endpoint (no API key required):

| Table | Content | Geography |
|---|---|---|
| 17-10-0149-01 | Components of population change (net migration outcomes) | CMA |
| 17-10-0148-01 | Population estimates (age structure) | CMA |
| 34-10-0133-01 | CMHC average rents | CMA |
| 14-10-0020-01 | Unemployment and participation rate | Province |
| 27-10-0273-02 | R&D expenditures by performing sector | Province |

After cleaning, the merged panel is **40 CMAs × 24 years = 960 observations**.
